name: axis-06-cooling-tower
version_tag: MECHANICAL CALENDAR AXIS — axis-05 BOSL2 parts + a SACRIFICIAL COOLING TOWER (Ron idea: reproduce why the bottom thread came out perfect — it shared every layer with the other objects, giving ~5.5s/layer for the fan to set the crests; the top printed ALONE above z28 and collapsed to the speed floor). cooling_tower.stl = solid dia10 x 97mm white pillar at [105,82], ~30mm from the bolt, 8mm brim, SNAP OFF AND DISCARD after. It gives the bolt top a travel-away destination AND enough per-layer path that slow_down_layer_time is actually reachable above slow_down_min_speed 12 (the real axis-05 flaw: a lone bolt-top ring hit the 12mm/s floor and finished in ~3s, so the 20s target was never met). With the tower the layer reaches the target above the floor, so slow_down_layer_time is dialed 20 -> 12 (still 2x the proven-good 5.5s bottom) and runtime drops accordingly. Everything else identical to axis-05: BOSL2 threads (pitch 2.5, 1.35mm radial, verified in mesh), SUPPORTS OFF (non-negotiable — supports pack the nut bore), outer wall 120 / accel 2000, 8mm brim, 4 walls. Tower brim (y69-95) clears bolt brim (y108-148). Discard the tower; keep bolt + 2 nuts.
